# setup


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

This module holds what must happen before a session starts. The terminal
session runs best inside tmux, a terminal multiplexer that divides one
window into panes. tmux gives Ramabana a split for the now pane, the
live view of the turn described in [pane](18_pane.ipynb). With the
extended keys setting on, tmux also delivers the alt keys and
`shift+enter` to the program as keys of their own. `shift+enter` arrives
only from a terminal that sends it. The first run therefore starts
Ramabana inside a tmux server of its own and offers to install tmux when
it is missing. `ramabana --doctor` reports what it found. The module
also decides whether the code index needs rebuilding.

## Extras and scripts

Every console script that the package installs starts in this module.
The module imports only fastcore and the standard library, and never
`ramabana.core`. A script starts quickly this way and can check for its
dependencies before it imports them.

`installed(mod)` says whether a module would import, without importing
it. `need(extra)` checks the modules of an extra, as listed in `EXTRAS`.
It returns `''` when all are installed. Otherwise it returns a message
that names the missing modules and gives the `pip install` command.
`SCRIPTS` names each console script other than `ramabana`, with the
module whose
[`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#main) it runs,
the extra it needs and the modules it needs. A lookup of one of these
names on this module returns that
[`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#main). When a
needed module is missing, the lookup returns a stand-in that prints the
message and exits with status 2. `follow_cmd(log, snap)` is the shell
line a transcript pane runs: the pane module following
[`log`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/peers.html#log) in the
palette of the snapshot `snap`, or `tail -f` when the terminal extra is
missing. `ramabana.core` re-exports
[`installed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#installed),
[`need`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#need),
`EXTRAS` and `SCRIPTS`.

## The config

Each session gets a tmux server of its own, started as
`tmux -L ramabana-<id>` with the config file `<cfg>/tmux.conf`. A new
server reads the current `tmux.conf` and inherits the current
environment. A second session therefore never picks up the first one’s
API keys or virtual environment. That server never reads `~/.tmux.conf`.
Your own tmux setup stays as it was.

Extended keys are a tmux setting that passes key combinations such as
`shift+enter` through to the program in the pane. Without it, tmux folds
them into plain `enter`. `tmux_conf(version)` returns the config for a
tmux version. It adds only the lines that version understands. An older
tmux prints an error for each line it does not know.
[`tmux_version`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#tmux_version)
reads the version from the output of `tmux -V`. The config claims true
colour (`RGB`) only when `$COLORTERM` says the terminal draws it. The
cell below prints the config for tmux 3.5.

</tr>

## The relaunch

[`Setup`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#setup)
collects everything about the tmux that Ramabana runs in: the config,
the relaunch into it, the install offer and `--doctor`.

[`Setup.launch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#setup.launch)
runs before an interactive session starts. Outside tmux it replaces the
current process with `tmux new-session` on a new server. The new session
runs the same command line in the same folder. Quitting Ramabana then
ends that tmux session and returns you to your shell. `launch` does
nothing in these cases: a one-shot prompt, `--json`, a stdin or stdout
that is not a terminal, and `--tmux off` or `$RAMABANA_TMUX=off`. It
also does nothing when `$RAMABANA_WRAPPED` is set, when tmux is older
than 3.0, and when tmux is missing and you decline the install offer.
The relaunched process has `$RAMABANA_WRAPPED` set. It never relaunches
a second time. Inside tmux, `--pane auto` then opens the now pane.

The server sets `destroy-unattached`, which ends the session when you
detach or close the window. Ramabana never keeps running where nobody
can see it. The history is saved, and `--resume latest` reopens it. The
command runs under `sh` with a short wrapper, `HOLD`. After a non-zero
exit, `HOLD` waits for enter. An error stays on screen instead of
vanishing with the tmux session. The command line goes to `HOLD` in
`$RAMABANA_ARGV`, not in the tmux arguments. The tmux client then does
not look like Ramabana to a tool that reads process arguments, such as
Sanketa. The pane process still runs `ramabana`.

Inside a tmux server of your own, `launch` turns `extended-keys` on for
that server when it is off. The change lasts until the server exits.
Only programs that ask for extended keys receive them.

Every effect on the outside world goes through an argument of
[`Setup`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#setup):
`which`, `system`, `run`, `execvpe`, `ask` and `isatty`, plus `environ`,
`argv` and `cwd`. The examples pass fakes for all of them. They run
without tmux and change nothing.

### prune_sockets

``` python
def prune_sockets(
    folder, # a tmux socket folder, `$TMUX_TMPDIR/tmux-<uid>`
    prefix:str='ramabana-', # only sockets whose names start with this
    age:int=5, # keep sockets younger than this many seconds: their server may still be starting
):
```

*Remove the sockets in `folder` that start with `prefix` and refuse a
connection; return their names.*

The example builds a fake machine, `Box`, that has tmux 3.5 on `PATH`
and records each command run, each question asked and the `execvpe` it
would make. `launch` reruns the command line on a new tmux server,
starting in `/work`, with `$RAMABANA_WRAPPED` set. The original command
line is in `$RAMABANA_ARGV` and not in the tmux arguments:

``` python
from types import SimpleNamespace
import shlex, tempfile

class Box:
    "Programs on PATH, the commands run, the prompts shown and the exec made."
    def __init__(self, have=('tmux',), version='tmux 3.5a', system='Darwin', answer='', ext='on'):
        self.have, self.version, self.system, self.answer, self.ext = set(have), version, system, answer, ext
        self.calls, self.asked, self.execd = [], [], None
    def which(self, name): return f'/bin/{name}' if name in self.have else None
    def run(self, cmd, **kw):
        self.calls.append(list(cmd))
        if 'install' in cmd: self.have.add('tmux')
        return SimpleNamespace(returncode=0, stdout={'-V': self.version, 'show': self.ext}.get(cmd[1], ''))
    def ask(self, q): return self.asked.append(q) or self.answer
    def execvpe(self, *a): self.execd = a

def mk(box, **kw):
    return Setup(tempfile.mkdtemp(), environ=kw.pop('environ', {'PATH': '/bin', 'TMUX_TMPDIR': tempfile.mkdtemp()}), argv=['-c', '--pane', 'on'], cwd='/work',
                 which=box.which, system=lambda: box.system, run=box.run, execvpe=box.execvpe, ask=box.ask, isatty=lambda: True)

box = Box()
mk(box).launch()
exe, argv, env = box.execd
test_eq((exe, env['RAMABANA_WRAPPED'], argv[argv.index('-c'):][:2], shlex.split(env['RAMABANA_ARGV'])[-2:]), ('/bin/tmux', '1', ['-c', '/work'], ['--pane', 'on']))
assert '--pane' not in argv
argv
```

    ['tmux',
     '-L',
     'ramabana-2258542c',
     '-f',
     '/tmp/tmplzycq9mb/tmux.conf',
     'new-session',
     '-s',
     'ramabana',
     '-c',
     '/work',
     'sh',
     '-c',
     'eval "set -- $RAMABANA_ARGV"; "$@" || { s=$?; printf "\\nramabana exited with status %s · enter closes this\\n" $s; read _; exit $s; }',
     'ramabana']

A one-shot prompt, `--json` and `--tmux off` stay in the current
terminal:

``` python
for kw in (dict(prompt='hi'), dict(as_json=True), dict(tmux='off')):
    box = Box()
    mk(box).launch(**kw)
    test_eq(box.execd, None)
```

Each relaunch starts a tmux server on a new socket. A tmux server leaves
its socket file behind when it exits, even after `tmux kill-server`.
`launch` calls
[`prune_sockets`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#prune_sockets)
before each relaunch.
[`prune_sockets`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#prune_sockets)
removes each `ramabana-` socket that refuses a connection, because no
server listens on it. It keeps live sockets and the sockets of other
programs. It also keeps a socket younger than `age` seconds, because a
server that is still starting refuses connections for a moment. An error
on one socket skips that socket and does not stop the launch. The
example binds one live socket and two dead sockets in a temporary
folder. The new dead socket stays until `age=0`:

``` python
import socket
```

``` python
d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp'))
socks = {n: socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX) for n in ('ramabana-live', 'ramabana-dead', 'mine')}
for n, s in socks.items(): s.bind(str(d/n))
socks['ramabana-live'].listen()
for n in ('ramabana-dead', 'mine'): socks[n].close()
test_eq(prune_sockets(d), [])
test_eq(prune_sockets(d, age=0), ['ramabana-dead'])
socks['ramabana-live'].close()
left = sorted(p.name for p in d.ls())
shutil.rmtree(d)
left
```

The `ramabana` script,
[`run_cli`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#run_cli),
makes the tmux decision before it imports the CLI. Importing the CLI
takes about 0.4 seconds. Deciding first lets the process outside tmux
hand over to tmux quickly. `launch_args(argv)` reads just enough of the
command line to know the session is interactive, without the full option
parser. It returns the `cfg` and `tmux` values that `launch` needs. It
returns `None` to leave the decision to
[`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#main) in the
CLI. It returns `None` for a prompt, for any option in `EARLY` (such as
`--json`, `--doctor` and `--help`), for `--tmux off`, for a valued
option with no value, and for options that
[`refusal`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#refusal)
rejects. An option it does not know is skipped.

[`refusal`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#refusal)
holds the checks that
[`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#main) makes
before it starts anything, such as `--pii` without `--vault`. It returns
the reason or `''`. Running it in
[`run_cli`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#run_cli)
refuses a bad option in your terminal and not on the tmux hold screen.
[`bare_resume`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#bare_resume)
gives a bare `--resume` the value `PICK_SESSION`, which lists this
folder’s sessions to choose from. When
[`run_cli`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#run_cli)
has called `launch`, it sets `LAUNCHED`.
[`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#main) then does
not call `launch` again.

## config.toml

`~/.config/ramabana/config.toml` holds this machine’s settings: one
file, edited by hand, that every Ramabana on the machine reads. A
session started with another `--cfg`, and an app that embeds Ramabana
with a config folder of its own, read the same file and never write into
their own folder for it. `$RAMABANA_CONFIG` names another file; the
tests use it.

A value can come from four places, and the first that has one wins:

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Source</th>
<th>Example</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>a command-line flag</td>
<td><code>--model gpt-5.4</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>an env var</td>
<td><code>$RAMABANA_MODEL</code>, or <code>$LEELA_MODEL</code> inside
Leela, the notebook editor that embeds Ramabana</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>config.toml</td>
<td><code>[jobs]</code> <code>turn = "gpt-5.4"</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>the built-in default</td>
<td><code>claude-opus-5-5</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`KEYS` lists every key: its type, the env var and the flag that beat it,
what it sets, and the values it may take. `drop_tools`, at the top
level, names the tools a session leaves out of the model’s schema. Each
tool’s schema costs tokens on every call. With no `drop_tools`, a
session keeps every tool. The tables are `[jobs]`, the model each job
runs on; `[window]`, the numbers the window guard works with;
`[compaction]`; `[runtime]`, what a model is started with; and `[cli]`,
the defaults of the terminal session’s flags that take a value.
`[jobs] image` is the OpenAI-compatible model `generate_image` draws
with. `[azure]` holds Azure OpenAI’s `endpoint`, which
`$AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` beats, read as named with no prefix
(`Key.plain`), and the `api_key_env` that names the env var holding its
key. A key an earlier release read, such as `azure.deployments`, is
reported with what to do instead (`RETIRED_KEYS`). A `[model."NAME"]`
table corrects the numbers fastllm’s table gives one model:
`max_input_tokens`, `max_output_tokens` and `supports_images`. Given
`model_id`, the same table defines a model of that name, with `runtime`,
`base_url`, `api_key_env`, `api_name`, `vendor_name` and `ctx`;
[core](core.html) registers it.

[`load_config`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#load_config)
reads the file again only when it changes. An entry it cannot use takes
its default and gives one warning, which
[`Agent.problems`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#agent.problems)
and `ramabana config show` repeat: a key nobody knows, with the nearest
one it might mean; a value of the wrong type or outside its choices; a
file that is not TOML. Nothing raises.

`keys.env`, beside `config.toml`, stores API keys saved by `/login`. A
name already in the environment wins over the file. The CLI loads
`keys.env` before any subcommand. The beat loads `beat.env` first and
`keys.env` second. A name in `beat.env` therefore wins in the beat.

A value beginning with `!` runs a shell command and uses its stripped
output, for example
`OPENAI_API_KEY=!security find-generic-password -ws openai` on macOS, or
`OPENAI_API_KEY=!op read op://vault/item/key`. A command that fails,
prints nothing or runs longer than 30 seconds leaves that name unset and
prints a warning on stderr. To store a value that begins with a literal
`!`, prefix it with `$`: `$!text` loads as `!text`.

Only the owner may read the file (`chmod 600`).
[`load_keys`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#load_keys)
refuses a file that other users can read and prints a warning on stderr.
Saved values are never printed or logged.

`ramabana setup` adds a provider’s model to `config.toml`. Use it when
no model runs yet, or when you want another provider. It prints
[`setup_guide`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#setup_guide)
from [core](core.html), which lists the providers and the model of each
job. It then lists the providers by number and asks for one. Azure
OpenAI, the AWS Bedrock Mantle endpoint and any OpenAI-compatible server
get a `[model."NAME"]` table, and `SETUP_FIELDS` says what each asks. A
provider whose models already have names, such as OpenAI or Claude Code,
needs only the model name. When no model runs here yet, the model
becomes the `turn` job in `[jobs]`. `--jobs` writes other jobs there.
Flags answer the same questions without a terminal. Without a terminal
and without `--provider`, the command prints the guide and exits with
status 2. It writes through
[`set_table`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#set_table),
which edits or adds one table and keeps every comment. It never writes a
key.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/setup.py#L731"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

*`ramabana setup peers` installs the peer hooks; `ramabana setup`: add a

(`--jobs` names others). Asks only on a terminal; never writes a key.*

``` python
import tomllib
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    p = Path(d)/'config.toml'; p.write_text('learning = false   # kept\n')
    set_table('jobs', {'turn': 'az'}, p); set_table('az', {'model_id': 'gpt-5.4'}, p)
    test_eq(tomllib.loads(p.read_text()), {'learning': False, 'jobs': {'turn': 'az'}, 'model': {'az': {'model_id': 'gpt-5.4'}}})
    assert '# kept' in p.read_text()
```

[`set_setting`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#set_setting)
writes one top-level key, such as `learning` or `pane_close_done`. It
rewrites that key’s line, or the commented-out line that the template
left. Every comment stays. A missing file starts from the template.
[`set_setting`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#set_setting)
refuses a file that is not valid TOML, says so in a `ValueError`, and
never rewrites the file.

``` python
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    p = Path(d)/'config.toml'
    test_eq(set_setting('learning', False, p), False)
    text = p.read_text()
    assert '\nlearning = false\n' in text
    test_eq(load_config(p), ({'learning': False}, []))
    set_setting('learning', True, p); test_eq(p.read_text().count('learning = '), 1)
    p.write_text('# mine\nlearning = [')
    try: set_setting('learning', False, p); raise AssertionError('rewrote a file it cannot read')
    except ValueError: pass
    test_eq(p.read_text(), '# mine\nlearning = [')
print(config_template()[:900])
```

`cli.read_outside` and `cli.vault` default to `false`. Their negative
flags turn them off even when `config.toml` turns them on. A custom
`--cfg` ignores these two config defaults. `cli.pii` defaults to `off`
and needs the vault: a `--pii` flag without `--vault` is refused, but a
`cli.pii` from the file is skipped when the session has no vault, so a
file written for vault sessions never stops a plain one. Any `--pii`,
`--pii off` included, beats the file, and a custom `--cfg` ignores it as
it ignores `cli.vault`. When it does apply, the startup line names it
among the defaults that came from `config.toml`.

[`run_cli`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#run_cli)
handles `ramabana config` before the session’s own options are parsed.
`ramabana config init` writes the template, with every key commented out
beside its default. It refuses to replace a file that exists unless you
give `--force`. With `--force` it keeps the old file as
`config.toml.bak` and carries its `learning` setting across.
`ramabana config show` prints each key’s value in effect and where it
came from. For a corrected window it also prints fastllm’s own number.
`ramabana config path` prints the file’s path.
`ramabana config set KEY VALUE` writes one key through
[`config_set`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#config_set).
`KEY` is a `KEYS` name or `model.NAME.key`. NAME is quoted when it holds
a dot, and the key is split from the right. `ramabana config models`
prints
[`models_table`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/core.html#models_table).
[`set_table`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#set_table)
writes a table that `KEYS` names, such as `runtime` or `subagents`,
under its own header. It treats any other table name as a model’s table.

``` python
import inspect
import ramabana.cli as _defaults_cli
import ramabana.setup as _defaults_setup
from unittest.mock import patch as _defaults_patch
```

``` python
import os
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    os.environ['RAMABANA_CONFIG'] = str(p := Path(d)/'config.toml')
    try:
        test_eq(config_cli(['init']), 0); test_eq(config_cli(['init']), 1)
        set_setting('learning', False)
        test_eq(config_cli(['init', '--force']), 0)
        assert (p.parent/'config.toml.bak').exists() and setting('learning') is False
        other = p.with_name('other.toml'); other.write_text('learning = false\n')   # a file that `setting` does not read
        config_reset(other); test_eq(load_config(other)[0].get('learning'), False)
        p.write_text(p.read_text().replace('# summary = ', 'summary = "gpt-5.4" #', 1))
        os.environ['RAMABANA_MODEL'] = 'gpt-5.4-mini'
        out = config_show()
        assert 'jobs.summary = "gpt-5.4"   # config.toml' in out and 'jobs.turn = "gpt-5.4-mini"   # $RAMABANA_MODEL' in out
        assert 'jobs.classify = "claude-haiku-5-5"   # built-in' in out
    finally: os.environ.pop('RAMABANA_CONFIG'); os.environ.pop('RAMABANA_MODEL', None)
print(out)
```

## Installing tmux

When tmux is missing, `offer_install` shows the install command and asks
once whether to run it. The command is `brew install tmux` on macOS, and
`sudo apt-get install -y tmux` or `sudo dnf install -y tmux` on Linux.
`installer` picks the command from what is on `PATH`. The command runs
attached to the terminal. `sudo` can therefore ask for a password.

`offer_install` stores the answer in `<cfg>/setup.json`. It never asks
again after a no, after a yes whose install worked, or when no install
command exists. Ctrl+c at the prompt and an install that failed or was
interrupted store nothing. The next run asks again. `ramabana --doctor`
asks even after an earlier no. Without tmux, the session starts in the
current terminal and prints one line on how to get the now pane.

The first example says yes on a Mac with Homebrew, and the session
relaunches in the tmux it installed. The second says no on Linux, and a
second `launch` does not ask again:

## Whether the code index needs to run

The `search_code` tool searches a code index that kosha builds over the
installed packages and the open folders. Rebuilding the index is called
a sync. A sync takes time. The session skips it when nothing the sync
reads has changed.

`index_gate(cfg, roots)` decides this without importing kosha.
[`index_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#index_state)
takes a fingerprint of what a sync would read. The fingerprint holds the
installed distributions that `importlib.metadata` finds, with their
modification times
([`pkg_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#pkg_state)).
For each folder it holds the git HEAD and a digest of `git status` with
the modification times of the paths it names
([`root_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#root_state)).
Outside git, a folder’s fingerprint hashes each visible file’s relative
path, size and nanosecond modification time, skipping hidden files and
folders.
[`index_gate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#index_gate)
returns the fingerprint and a reason to run kosha, or `''` to skip the
sync. The reason is `''` when the fingerprint matches the one that the
last good sync saved in `<cfg>/kosha-state.json`, and each folder’s
`.kosha/code.db` and kosha’s package database,
[`kosha_env_db()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#kosha_env_db),
exist. When the fingerprint matches and a database is missing, the
reason is `index missing`. Otherwise
[`index_changes`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#index_changes)
says what changed, such as `packages changed: +foo 1.2`.

After a good sync the session calls
[`save_index`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#save_index)
to store the new fingerprint. Either way
[`log_index`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#log_index)
appends one line to `<cfg>/kosha.log`, and `--doctor` shows the last
line through
[`last_index`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#last_index).
The example walks a fresh folder through a first sync, a missing index,
an unchanged state and a new package:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/setup.py#L925"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
import tempfile
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d); (site := d/'site').mkdir(); (site/'fastcore-1.8.0.dist-info').mkdir(); (root := d/'proj').mkdir()
    state, why = index_gate(d/'cfg', [root], [site])
    test_eq((list(state['packages']), why), (['fastcore-1.8.0'], 'first sync'))
    save_index(d/'cfg', state)
    test_eq(index_gate(d/'cfg', [root], [site])[1], 'index missing')
    (root/'.kosha').mkdir(); (root/'.kosha'/'code.db').write_text('')
    if kosha_env_db().exists(): test_eq(index_gate(d/'cfg', [root], [site])[1], '')
    (site/'foo-1.2.dist-info').mkdir()
    assert index_gate(d/'cfg', [root], [site])[1].endswith('packages changed: +foo 1.2')
    log_index(d/'cfg', 'skip', 'unchanged', .01)
    test_eq(last_index(d/'cfg').split(' · ')[1:], ['skip', 'unchanged', '0.01s'])
```

## Peer hooks

`ramabana setup peers` puts the peer hooks of
[peer_hooks](25_peer_hooks.ipynb) and the `peer-work` text of
[peer_work](24_peer_work.ipynb) into the config of Claude Code and
Codex, so those sessions can talk to each other and to Ramabana. It
never writes before you say yes. For each agent it prints a unified diff
of every file it would change, then asks once. `--yes` skips the
question. `--remove` takes out only what this command put in.

The hooks go into the `hooks` table of `~/.claude/settings.json` and
`~/.codex/hooks.json`. Each hook command is the full path of this Python
with `-m ramabana.peer_hooks`, so it runs this ramabana whatever is
first on `PATH`. A hook group is ours when one of its commands has
`ramabana.peer_hooks` or `peer-hook` in it, so the `ramabana peer-hook`
groups of older setups are replaced or removed too. A second run
replaces our groups where they stand and changes nothing when they are
equal. Your own hooks and settings stay as they are. If the file is not
valid JSON, the command names it and writes nothing for that agent.

[`merge_hooks`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#merge_hooks)
does the merge. An empty block removes our groups, and an event with no
groups left is dropped:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/setup.py#L941"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### merge_hooks

``` python
def merge_hooks(
    cfg, block
):
```

*`cfg` with our hook groups set to `block` (by event) where ours stood;
empty `block` removes them.*

``` python
theirs = {'hooks': [{'type': 'command', 'command': 'notify-me'}]}
ours = lambda e: {'hooks': [{'type': 'command', 'command': f'ramabana peer-hook claude {e}'}]}
cfg = {'model': 'opus', 'hooks': {'Stop': [theirs, ours('stop'), theirs]}}
new = merge_hooks(cfg, {'Stop': [ours('stop2')], 'End': [ours('end')]})
test_eq(new, {'model': 'opus', 'hooks': {'Stop': [theirs, ours('stop2'), theirs], 'End': [ours('end')]}})
test_eq(merge_hooks(new, {'Stop': [ours('stop2')], 'End': [ours('end')]}), new)
test_eq(merge_hooks(new, {}), {'model': 'opus', 'hooks': {'Stop': [theirs, theirs]}})
test_eq(merge_hooks({'hooks': {'Stop': [ours('stop')]}}, {}), {})
new_form = {'hooks': [{'type': 'command', 'command': '/usr/bin/python3 -m ramabana.peer_hooks claude stop'}]}
test_eq([_ours(g) for g in (ours('stop'), new_form, theirs, 'odd')], [True, True, False, False])
test_eq(merge_hooks({'hooks': {'Stop': [theirs, ours('stop')]}}, {'Stop': [new_form]}), {'hooks': {'Stop': [theirs, new_form]}})
```

## The text and the files

Claude Code reads a skill from `~/.claude/skills/peer-work/SKILL.md`.
[`peer_skill`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#peer_skill)
gives it the docstring of `peer_work` under front matter that names the
skill. Codex has no skills, but it reads `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`, which is
your own file. For Codex the text is one section between two marker
lines. A new run replaces that section and no other part. `--remove`
takes out that section only, and deletes the file only when nothing else
is left in it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/setup.py#L952"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### peer_skill

``` python
def peer_skill(
    kind
):
```

*The peer-work text for agent `kind`: a Claude Code skill file, or the
marked section of Codex’s `AGENTS.md`.*

``` python
mine = '# Mine\n\nBe brief.\n'
once = _section(mine, peer_skill('codex'))
test_eq(_section(once, peer_skill('codex')), once)
test_eq(_section(once + '\nAfter.\n', ''), mine + '\nAfter.\n')
test_eq(_section(once, ''), mine)
assert peer_skill('claude').startswith('---\nname: peer-work\ndescription: The rules')
```

## The command

[`setup_peers`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#setup_peers)
plans the changes of each agent as `(path, text now, text after)`,
prints a diff of each one that differs, and asks. A missing file has no
text now, and is made on write. A text after of `None` deletes the file.
The folders are made on write, and `home` replaces `~`, so a test never
touches your real config.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/setup.py#L1005"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### setup_peers

``` python
def setup_peers(
    argv, ask:function=_no_stdin, out:builtin_function_or_method=print, home:NoneType=None
):
```

*`ramabana setup peers [--agent claude|codex|all] [--remove] [--yes]`:
show each file’s diff, write after a yes; 0, or 1 when something was
refused.*

``` python
import tempfile
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    shown = []
    test_eq(setup_peers(['--agent', 'claude'], ask=lambda q: 'n', out=shown.append, home=d), 1)
    assert shown[0].startswith(f'--- {d}/.claude/settings.json (now)') and not (Path(d)/'.claude').exists()
    test_eq(setup_peers(['--agent', 'claude', '--yes'], out=shown.append, home=d), 0)
    assert '"SessionStart"' in (Path(d)/'.claude/settings.json').read_text()
    test_eq(setup_peers(['--agent', 'claude', '--remove', '--yes'], out=shown.append, home=d), 0)
    test_eq(json.loads((Path(d)/'.claude/settings.json').read_text()), {})
```

Each agent has a line in `--doctor`.
[`peers_status`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#peers_status)
reads the hook command in the config of the agent and runs it the way
the agent would, but with no `PATH`, for the cheap event `version`. A
command that works shows the Python it runs and the ramabana version. A
command that fails, such as `ramabana peer-hook` from an older setup,
says why and how to fix it.
[`path_check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#path_check)
asks the `ramabana` on `PATH` for its version in the same cheap way.
When it is missing or reports another version, it gives one line that
says how to fix it, because an agent that types `ramabana tell` gets
that one:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/setup.py#L1047"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### path_check

``` python
def path_check(
    home:NoneType=None, which:function=which
):
```

*A line when the `ramabana` on `PATH` is missing or reports a version
other than the one the hooks run, else None.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/setup.py#L1033"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


*One line for each agent: whether its config has the peer hooks and what
they run, or how to install or fix them.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/setup.py#L1026"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### hook_check

``` python
def hook_check(
    cmd, home
):
```

*Run hook command `cmd` with the event `version`, with no `PATH`, as a
check: (True, the ramabana version) or (False, why it fails).*

``` python
from ramabana import __version__
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    test_eq(peers_status(d), [f'peers: {k} hooks not installed: run ramabana setup peers --agent {k}' for k in ('claude', 'codex')])
    setup_peers(['--agent', 'codex', '--yes'], out=lambda s: None, home=d)
    test_eq(peers_status(d)[1], f'peers: codex hooks installed (runs: {sys.executable}, ramabana {__version__})')
    (Path(d)/'.claude').mkdir(); (Path(d)/'.claude/settings.json').write_text(json.dumps({'hooks': {'Stop': [{'hooks': [{'type': 'command', 'command': 'ramabana peer-hook claude stop'}]}]}}))
    assert peers_status(d)[0].startswith('peers: claude hook command fails: ')
    fake = Path(d)/'ramabana'
    fake.write_text('#!/bin/sh\necho 0.0.1\n'); fake.chmod(0o755)
    assert 'is 0.0.1; the hooks run' in path_check(d, lambda n: fake)
    fake.write_text(f'#!/bin/sh\necho {__version__}\n')
    test_eq(path_check(d, lambda n: fake), None)
    assert 'uv tool install' in path_check(d, lambda n: None)
```

## `--doctor`

`ramabana --doctor` prints one line for each thing the now pane and the
keys depend on: the tmux version, whether it can split a pane (tmux 3.1
or later), extended keys, the config file, `ramabana-pane`, the missing
extras, the code index’s last decision, and one line for each agent that
peer talk can reach: whether its config has the peer hooks. A line from
[`path_check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#path_check)
follows when the `ramabana` on `PATH` is missing or reports another
version. It then prints a getting-started checklist. When tmux is
missing it also offers to install it, even after an earlier no. The
example runs it on a fake machine with tmux 3.0, which is too old for
the split:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/setup.py#L1056"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Setup.doctor

``` python
def doctor():
```

*Print one line per check, offer to install tmux when it is missing, and
return 0.*

``` python
mk(Box(have={'tmux', 'ramabana-pane'}, version='tmux 3.0a')).doctor()
```
